xna-type.name: ContentManager
xna-type.summary: The ContentManager is the run-time component which loads managed objects from the binary files produced by the design time content pipeline. It also manages the lifespan of the loaded objects, disposing the content manager will also dispose any assets which are themselves IDisposable.

constructor.summary: Initializes a new instance of ContentManager.

parameters.parameter: The service provider that the ContentManager should use to locate services.

constructor.remarks: Warning When creating a new ContentManager , if no instance of Game is otherwise required by the application, it is often better to create a new class that implements the IServiceProvider interface rather than creating an instance of Game just to create a new instance of GraphicsDeviceManager . By default, the ContentManager searches for content in the directory where the executable is located.

method.name: Load
method.summary: Loads an asset that has been processed by the Content Pipeline.

overload.summary: Loads an asset that has been processed by the Content Pipeline.

type-parameters.type-parameter: The type of asset to load. Model , Effect , SpriteFont , Texture , Texture2D and TextureCube are all supported by default by the standard Content Pipeline processor, but additional types may be loaded by extending the processor.

parameters.parameter: Asset name, relative to the loader root directory, and not including the .xnb file extension.

overload.returns: The loaded asset. Repeated calls to load the same asset will return the same object instance.

exceptions.exception: Load was called after the ContentManager was disposed.
The type of the assetName in the file does not match the type of asset requested as specified by T.

overload.remarks: Before a ContentManager can load an asset, you need to add the asset to your game project using the steps described in How to: Add a Resource to the Content Pipeline . The following are the Content Pipeline run-time classes supported by Load and the file formats they are associated with. Effect Class .fx Model Class .fbx, .x SpriteFont Class .bmp, .spritefont Note The default content processor for .bmp files is the texture processor. To process a .bmp file for use as a Sprite Font, click Sprite Font Texture - XNA Framework in the Properties pane for the .bmp file after it has been added to the project. Texture Class , Texture2D Class , TextureCube Class .bmp, .dds, .dib, .hdr, .jpg, .pfm, .png, .ppm, and .tga Note that these are the formats of the original assets; after processing, all assets will be .xnb files.

exceptions.exception: Unable to open the file containing assetName, or the file was not found.

method.name: ReadAsset
method.summary: Low-level worker method that reads asset data.

overload.summary: Low-level worker method that reads asset data.
overload.syntax: protected T ReadAsset<T> ( string assetName, Action<IDisposable> recordDisposableObject )

type-parameters.type-parameter: Type of the asset specified for loading.

parameters.parameter: The name of the asset to be loaded from disk.

Delegate function for handling the disposition of assets. If is null , the default lifespan tracking and management is used, so unloading or disposing of the content manager frees everything that has been loaded through it. If specifies a valid delegate, that delegate is used instead of the default lifespan tracking and is called every time the loader encounters a type that implements IDisposable . You must use your own code to unload assets loaded in this fashion, since ContentManager 's Unload method will not be aware of them.

exceptions.exception: ReadAsset was called after the ContentManager was disposed.

overload.remarks: This protected method loads an .xnb file from disk. Unlike ContentManager 's public Load method, it always returns a new copy of the specified asset, even if the asset has been loaded previously. You can customize how shared assets are managed by overriding ContentManager 's Load method. In your own Load method, keep track of what has been loaded, and call ReadAsset when you need a new asset from disk.
